items.quote: If you only want to read your own company's data, you still need to set up an app — Intuit does not offer per-user API keys.
items.why: Implies no per-user keys, but never states OAuth2 as the auth method.
Names the accounting scope string only; doesn't state the auth method.

items.quote: A Node.js client for Intuit's OAuth 2.0 implementation.
items.why: Says Intuit has an OAuth 2.0 client library, not that the API uses oauth2.

items.quote: The Intuit Developer Portal rejects http://localhost redirect URIs in production mode.
items.why: Redirect URI rule in production mode; says nothing about approval or access gating.
Sandbox authorization fragment; nothing on production keys or approval.

items.quote: The QuickBooks Online Java SDK provides a set of Java class libraries that make it easier to call QuickBooks Online APIs
items.why: Java SDK description; no REST breadth, entity count, or tool count.

items.quote: This MCP server provides complete QuickBooks Online API integration for Claude Code and other MCP-compatible clients.
items.why: Marketing line about MCP integration; no REST entity breadth or 145-tool count.

items.quote: This server uses OAuth 2.0 to authenticate to a QuickBooks Online company.
items.why: Describes an OAuth2-authenticated server, implying it exists; no vendor-official statement.

items.quote: A comprehensive Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for QuickBooks Online
items.why: Confirms a comprehensive QBO MCP server exists; does not say Intuit/vendor-official.
